solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One left in a lot of murkiness, being lazy?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
a lot of, not all, so the word is cut short, keeping only its first part

parts.note: dinginess is gloomy murkiness

explanation.surface: Someone lounging in a gloomy fog, wondering if that counts as laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims DINGINESS to DING; 'in' puts L inside it, giving DLING, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idling is passing time doing nothing, which is a lazy way to behave; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Repeatedly, Las Vegan's behind favoured hitman

parts.note: repeatedly asks for the same bottom a second time, so it supplies another copy
an American's behind is an ass, the US word for arse
in favour, popular, is IN

explanation.surface: A Las Vegas mobster's backside, and a favoured hitman, in gangland Nevada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Las Vegan's' just signals the American word ASS rather than British ARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer hired or sent to murder a target, a hitman by another name.

clue.text: Wild place with tree containing cold box, maybe

indicators.note: containing means the scrambled letters hold the next piece
wild suggests the letters of the two words are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A wild spot with a tree in it, holding a chilly box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the letters to give REEPTACLE; 'containing' then holds C, so the box is the definition, not the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any container, and a box is one example, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Last pair in extravaganza notably on the fringes are clownish

indicators.note: the last pair in a word means its final two letters
the fringes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A lavish show whose edges are notably clownish.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany describes comically eccentric, slapstick behaviour, like a clown's antics.

clue.text: Working sort first off with stamps welcoming latest of clientele?

definitions.text: Working sort first off with stamps welcoming latest of clientele?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order
first off says the opening letter of the word is removed
latest of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A worker at the post office, stamps in hand, greeting the newest customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' removes S from SORT, leaving ORT; 'welcoming' brings in E, the last of 'clientele', to join STAMPS; 'Working' rearranges the lot. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmaster runs a post office, a working figure dealing in stamps and serving customers.

clue.text: Skirt pleated generally? Not altogether

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about whether a skirt is pleated all over, answered 'not entirely'.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt is to go round the border of something, and an edge is that border; both noun senses also match.

clue.text: A week taken in African country or another

indicators.note: taken in means these letters are put inside the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A week spent visiting one African country, or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' looks like the definition but supplies MALI; 'another' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a further African nation in the south-east, so it is 'another' besides Mali.

clue.text: British colleague with short catchy phrase creates commotion

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or partner

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a hook is the catchy phrase of a song

explanation.surface: A British co-worker with a snappy slogan stirs up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss and hype, a synonym for commotion.

clue.text: Reckless sort varying speed, source of renewed commotion

indicators.note: varying tells us the letters of the word are changed around
the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A reckless driver changing speed causes yet more commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw who will take any risk.

clue.text: Staged production backed in Birmingham ardently

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A play performed with enthusiastic support in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters AMARD inside 'Birmingham ardently'; 'backed' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a piece put on stage in performance.

clue.text: A poet might use this independent publication linked to English network

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication
RY, railway, is a network of lines

explanation.surface: An independent magazine tied in with an English broadcasting network, something a poet would use.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is vivid descriptive language, the pictures in words that poets work with.

clue.text: Note terrible trouble for subject of pedicurist's attention?

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A note about a dreadful problem with one's feet, for the chiropodist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicurist cares for feet, so a toenail is one thing they trim and treat.

clue.text: Cut endlessly vapid chatter

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut short endless empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is informal for idle, empty talk, so it matches vapid chatter.

clue.text: Two that stir in a haphazard way initially

indicators.note: haphazard means random, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people who stir things up at random from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To start with' is an idiom meaning at first, at the beginning.

clue.text: Cricket ground features this small centre attended by executives

parts.note: the core is the centre
a board is a group of company executives

explanation.surface: A cricket ground's small central area visited by company bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ground displays the runs and wickets on a big scoreboard.

clue.text: Get unjustified blame with secure diplomat entering hidden danger

parts.note: to secure something is to take it

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a trap is a hidden danger
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy walking into a concealed peril and being wrongly blamed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the rap is an idiom for being punished for something someone else did.

clue.text: Boost too in pitch after regular cancellations

indicators.note: cancelling letters at regular intervals leaves every other one

explanation.surface: A singer told to boost their pitch, too, after shows were repeatedly called off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that lifts the spirits or gives a boost.

clue.text: Egyptian ruler held unrestricted period for instruction

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, was a pharaoh of Egypt

indicators.note: unrestricted means the word's outer letters, its restraints, are removed

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A pharaoh kept in for a long period of teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrestricted' strips the outer letters of 'held', leaving EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guidance and teaching, as from a tutor.

clue.text: Maybe, caught striking

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman caught is one way of being ...

explanation.definitionFit: Out covers a batsman dismissed, such as by a catch, and workers who have stopped work in a strike.

clue.text: Artist close to park and a house bordering lake

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
bordering means these letters wrap around the next one

explanation.surface: A painter near a park, with a house beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter, famous for her self-portraits.

clue.text: Something on top European chap for broadcast gets unwelcome feedback

parts.note: a hat is something worn on top of the head

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like this one

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A European man on air, wearing a hat, receives abusive letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is hostile messages sent to someone, very unwelcome responses.

clue.text: A street cred ruined? It's not something professionals divulge

indicators.note: ruined suggests the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone's street cred is ruined by a professional who blabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade secret is a method a business or craft keeps private from outsiders.

clue.text: Greatly respect Democrat put in a complicated situation

indicators.note: put in means this letter goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a mire is a messy, difficult situation

explanation.surface: Respect for a Democrat who is in a real mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard.

clue.text: Brass instrument lacking a container

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: the tuba is a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: A brass instrument with no case to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is an open vessel, a kind of container.

clue.text: One not being straight with set of engineers in ancient craft

parts.note: bi, short for bisexual, describes someone who is not straight
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone bent, among army engineers, on an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Complaint from fancy mogul boarding airline? The opposite!

indicators.note: boarding would put the scrambled letters into the airline
the opposite reverses that, so the airline goes inside the scrambled letters
fancy suggests an elaborate reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: A tycoon boarding a flight, or the plane boarding the tycoon, ends in back trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' gives LUMGO; 'boarding' alone would put that inside the airline, but 'The opposite!' flips it so the airline sits inside, after LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is lower back pain, a complaint in the medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: A secret place of illegal activity somewhere in the Arab world

parts.note: a den, as in a den of thieves, is a hideout for crime

explanation.surface: A hidden criminal hideout somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, in the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Ship pilot circles in the morning

indicators.note: circles means these letters go round the others

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A ship's pilot circling round in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, a vessel driven by steam.

clue.text: See red photograph

explanation.definitionFit: Snap means to lose one's temper abruptly, and also a quick snapshot picture.

clue.text: Board game about to include first of some prickly stuff

parts.note: Go is an ancient board game from East Asia

indicators.note: to include means these letters go around the next one

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A board game about to bring in something spiky.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, a very prickly plant.

clue.text: Manager is altering a set of free market beliefs?

definitions.text: a set of free market beliefs?

indicators.note: altering tells us the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager is changing a set of free-market convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaganism was Ronald Reagan's economic policy of tax cuts and deregulation, a free-market creed.
